items.longBusinessSummary: Cameco Corporation provides uranium for the generation of electricity in the Americas, Europe, and Asia. It operates in three segments: Uranium, Fuel Services, and Westinghouse. The Uranium segment engages in the exploration for, mining, milling, purchase, and sale of uranium concentrate. Its Fuel Services segment is involved in the refining, conversion, and fabrication of uranium concentrate, as well as purchase and sale of conversion services. The Westinghouse segment operates as a nuclear reactor technology original equipment manufacturer and a provider of products and services to commercial utilities and government agencies. It also provides outage and maintenance, engineering support, instrumentation and controls equipment, and plant modification services, as well as components and parts to nuclear reactors. The company sells its uranium and fuel products and services to nuclear utilities. Cameco Corporation was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Saskatoon, Canada.

Title: Purecore Publishes Uranium Market Report Tracking AI-Driven Nuclear Demand
Author: Purecore Metals Inc.   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:30 PM GMT+1 7 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T11:30:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Purecore Metals Inc. (CSE: PURE) (FSE: J8Y) (OTCQB: PPURF) ("Purecore" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the publication of Uranium and the AI Power Boom, a comprehensive industry report examining projected global uranium supply and demand against the backdrop of accelerating electricity consumption from artificial intelligence ("AI") and data centre infrastructure.
The report draws on data from the International Energy Agency ("IEA"), International Atomic Energy Agency ("IAEA"), U.S. Energy Information Administration ("EIA"), Sprott Asset Management, Cameco Corporation and other recognized industry sources. It highlights a timing imbalance between the rapid development of AI infrastructure and the longer development timelines associated with new uranium mines.
Please download the free report here: Download report (www.purecoremetals.com/uranium-report/)
Uranium and the AI Power Boom — Report Highlights
The report examines several developments influencing the global uranium industry:
AI-Driven Electricity Demand: The IEA's projection that data centre electricity consumption could reach 950 TWh annually by 2030.1
Global Nuclear Expansion: The IAEA's latest nuclear generating-capacity projections through 2060.3
Long-Term Uranium Supply: Industry scenarios indicating cumulative uranium supply deficits of approximately 700 M to 1.7 Blb of U₃O₈ through 2040.4
Uranium Pricing: September 2026 industry-average spot and long-term indicators of US$89.63 and US$96.50/lb, respectively.5
Nuclear Utility Contracting: EIA data showing approximately 186.3 Mlb of unfilled U.S. utility requirements for 2026–2035.6
Global Production Concentration: Kazakhstan's approximately 40% share of global uranium mine production.7
Exploration and Development: Long timelines associated with bringing new mining projects into production.2
Purecore's Portfolio: The Yurchison Uranium Property in Saskatchewan and Bankier Property in British Columbia.
Peter Berdusco, President and CEO of Purecore, commented:
"Artificial intelligence is introducing another powerful source of electricity demand. The world's largest technology companies are increasingly looking toward nuclear energy as a source of reliable, around-the-clock power capable of supporting the scale and performance requirements of next-generation data centres. We compiled this report because we believe investors should have access to the same underlying industry data that informs our strategic decisions. Understanding the relationship between nuclear expansion, uranium supply and long-term electricity demand is fundamental to understanding why Purecore is building its portfolio around uranium and other critical minerals."
Purecore's Uranium and Critical Minerals Strategy
Purecore continues to pursue an acquisition- and exploration-focused strategy targeting uranium and copper opportunities in prospective mining jurisdictions.
The Company's Yurchison Uranium Property, located in the Wollaston Domain of northern Saskatchewan, comprises 22 mineral claims covering approximately 35,029 hectares. Pursuant to its definitive option agreement with Skyharbour Resources Ltd., Purecore holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in Yurchison.9
The property is located approximately 75 kilometres south of Cameco's Rabbit Lake operation and is the subject of an ongoing historical data compilation and technical review program intended to support future exploration target generation.9
Through its existing portfolio and ongoing evaluation of additional opportunities, Purecore aims to build a portfolio of critical mineral exploration assets positioned within the broader themes of nuclear energy expansion, electrification and increasing global electricity requirements.
Global Nuclear Expansion and Uranium Supply
The IAEA's September 2026 nuclear power projections provide additional evidence of the potential scale of future nuclear energy expansion. According to the IAEA, approximately 413 nuclear reactors were operating worldwide at the end of 2025, representing 377.1 gigawatts of electrical generating capacity.3
Under the agency's high-growth scenario, global nuclear generating capacity could increase to approximately 1,045 gigawatts by 2050 and 1,284 gigawatts by 2060, more than three times the 2025 operating capacity. These figures are scenario-based projections, not assured outcomes.3
Sprott's uranium market analysis estimates that cumulative uranium supply deficits could approach 700 Mlb of U₃O₈ by 2040 under its underlying demand assumptions. Under a scenario incorporating global net-zero commitments, the projected cumulative deficit could reach approximately 1.7 Blb of U₃O₈ over the same period.4
According to Cameco's published uranium pricing data, the industry-average uranium spot price was US$89.63/lb U₃O₈ at September 30, 2026, compared with US$24.63/lb in January 2020. The industry-average long-term uranium price indicator was US$96.50/lb at September 30, 2026, compared with US$35.00/lb at the end of 2020.5
The report examines how outstanding U.S. nuclear utility contracting requirements, together with potential global nuclear fleet expansion, could influence uranium procurement strategies and future demand for primary uranium production.
Concentration of Global Uranium Production
According to the World Nuclear Association, Kazakhstan accounted for approximately 40% of global uranium mine production in 2025, making it the world's largest uranium-producing country.7
Kazatomprom, Kazakhstan's national uranium company and the world's largest uranium producer, reported that its attributable production represented approximately 20% of global primary uranium production in 2025.8
Numbers in the text refer to the sources below. Third-party projections are scenarios, not guarantees.

Title: Cameco vs. Centrus vs. BWX Technologies: Ranking the 3 Nuclear Stocks That Get Paid Before a Reactor Is Built.
Author: Leo Sun, The Motley Fool   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 9:25 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T20:25:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Cameco (NYSE: CCJ), Centrus (NYSE: LEU), and BWX Technologies (NYSE: BWXT) are all linchpins of the nuclear energy market. Cameco is one of the world's largest uranium miners; Centrus is a major uranium enricher, and BWX builds crucial nuclear components.
In theory, all three companies should benefit from the nuclear market's recent resurgence -- which was driven by new decarbonization initiatives, safer nuclear technologies, and the expansion of the power-hungry cloud infrastructure and AI markets. But over the past 12 months, Cameco's stock fell 8%, BWX's dipped 7%, and Centrus' plummeted 72%. Let's see why these three nuclear stocks fizzled out -- and which one is the best turnaround play.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
Cameco, based in Canada, is the world's second-largest uranium miner after Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom (OTC:NATK.Y). It operates mines in Canada, the U.S., and Kazakhstan. It also owns nearly half of Westinghouse Electric, one of the world's top nuclear plant builders, and Global Laser Enrichment (GLE), its uranium enrichment joint venture with Silex (OTC: SILXY).
Cameco still generates most of its revenue from mining. Still, its investments in Westinghouse and GLE could eventually turn it into a "one-stop shop" for mining, converting, and selling enriched uranium. Instead of selling its uranium at spot prices (which would expose it to more volatility), Cameco locks most of its clients into long-term, partly fixed-price contracts. That approach is safer, but it also limits Cameco's exposure to rising uranium prices.
Centrus is one of the few U.S. companies licensed to sell low-enriched uranium (LEU), the most common fuel for commercial nuclear reactors. It's also the only public U.S. company authorized to sell high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for next-gen reactors.
Centrus once enriched its own uranium, but it shut down its domestic plants over a decade ago when it became cheaper to import and sell overseas LEU. But in recent years, the sanctions against Russia and the U.S. government's push toward energy independence have driven Centrus to restart its LEU plant in Ohio and begin producing HALEU in the United States. That transformation from a middleman to a first-party producer is squeezing its near-term margins.
BWX is the only large-scale producer of specialized nuclear components, fuel systems, and naval reactor systems in North America. It's one of the few companies authorized to work with regulated nuclear materials, handle HALEU and tri-structural isotropic (TRISO) fuel, and develop naval reactor components for the U.S. Navy. It also produces tiny microreactors, which are cooled by gas rather than water and generate approximately 1-5 MWe.
BWX generates most of its revenue from the defense sector, so it's better insulated from the macro headwinds than commercial-oriented nuclear companies. Its scale and diversification also keep it more profitable than smaller next-gen reactor makers.
Rising interest rates pose the biggest near-term threat for all three companies, because they could throttle economic growth and compress their valuations. But over the next few years, analysts clearly expect BWX to grow faster than Cameco and Centrus.
Cameco's growth rates are steady, but its conservatively hedged contracts limit its long-term growth potential compared to producers that directly sell their uranium at spot prices. Centrus' earnings will decline through 2028 as it restarts its capital-intensive domestic plants and ramps up HALEU production, but those investments should pay off in the long run.
BWX is better positioned to profit from the nuclear market's near-term growth. It's better diversified, it controls a crucial link of the North American nuclear supply chain, and the growth of its defense business should insulate it from the next recession.
In addition to growing faster over the next few years, BWX's stock also trades at a lower forward multiple than Cameco and Centrus. While that might seem like an apples-to-oranges comparison, BWX is clearly the safer overall play on the ongoing nuclear boom.
Before you buy stock in Cameco, consider this:
The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Cameco wasn't one of them. The 10 stocks that made the cut could produce monster returns in the coming years.
Consider when Netflix made this list on December 17, 2004... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you'd have $355,124!* Or when Nvidia made this list on April 15, 2005... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you'd have $1,296,254!*
Now, it's worth noting Stock Advisor's total average return is 901% — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 210% for the S&P 500. Don't miss the latest top 10 list, available with Stock Advisor, and join an investing community built by individual investors for individual investors.
*Stock Advisor returns as of October 26, 2026.
Leo Sun has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends BWX Technologies and Cameco. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

Title: Azincourt Energy Advances Labrador Uranium Exploration With New Snegamook Drilling Results
Author: Attiya Zainib   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:39 PM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T21:39:11+00:00
=== BODY ===
Azincourt Energy Corp. (TSX.V:AAZ) (OTC:AZURF) (FSE:A0U0) is continuing to evaluate the resource potential of its Snegamook uranium deposit in Labrador, Canada, after new drilling results identified additional mineralized intervals and helped refine targets for the next phase of exploration.
The company has completed four diamond drill holes totaling 1,069 meters at Snegamook, part of its Harrier Project in Labrador's Central Mineral Belt. The program is focused on verifying historical uranium discoveries and building the geological data needed to determine whether the deposit can support a maiden mineral resource estimate.
Recent results from two holes provided further evidence of uranium mineralization. Hole SN0048 intersected 19 meters grading 0.03% equivalent uranium oxide (eU₃O₈) within a broader 31.6-meter zone of elevated radioactivity. Hole SN0047 returned narrower mineralized intervals, including 0.8 meters grading 0.03% eU₃O₈. The results are helping the company assess the extent and continuity of mineralization identified in earlier drilling.
Azincourt's current campaign builds on promising historical results at the property. Previous drilling at hole SN-08-06 returned 0.97% U₃O₈ over 0.5 meters, while a selective check sample collected from the same area in 2025 graded 2.71% U₃O₈ over 10 centimeters. The company cautions that the short sample is not necessarily representative of the grade or width of the broader mineralized interval. The latest program also includes a hole drilled alongside historical hole SN-08-24, which previously intersected 0.05% U₃O₈ over 20 meters.
One important caveat is that the latest reported grades are preliminary radiometric estimates derived from downhole gamma measurements, rather than laboratory assay results. Samples have been collected for laboratory testing, with results expected in early 2027. Reported intersection lengths are measured along the drill holes, and true widths have not yet been established.
The company now expects to complete approximately 1,800 meters of drilling across six to seven holes during the 2026 program. In addition to testing known mineralization, Azincourt is reviewing historical drill core and plans to work with an independent qualified person to evaluate the available data. The objective is to establish whether the historical results can be verified and whether sufficient geological information exists to support a compliant mineral resource estimate.
Snegamook's location adds to its exploration appeal. The deposit sits approximately 1.3 kilometers southeast of the Two Time uranium deposit, where historical work outlined a resource of 6.1 million pounds of U₃O₈. Both areas contain uranium mineralization associated with altered and fractured rock formations, although the geological similarities do not establish the size or economic potential of the Snegamook deposit.
The broader Central Mineral Belt hosts several known uranium deposits, including Paladin Energy's Michelin project, and has attracted renewed exploration interest as companies and governments focus on securing long-term uranium supplies. However, uranium production has not yet begun in the region, and further exploration is needed to establish the commercial potential of individual projects.
For Azincourt, the next key milestones are laboratory assay results, continued drilling, and verification of the historical data. A maiden resource estimate remains a potential future objective rather than an established outcome. The results of the ongoing work should provide a clearer picture of whether Snegamook can advance beyond exploration and become a more defined asset within the company's uranium portfolio.
Uranium stocks like Cameco Corporation (CCJ), Centrus Energy Corp (LEU), Uranium Energy Corp (UEC), and NexGen Energy (NXE) were flying high earlier this year but CCJ lost more than 40% since hitting its 52-week high in January. Centrus Energy (LEU)'s 52 week loss is around 75%. Uranium Energy (UEC) lost nearly two thirds of its value since hitting its 52-week high in January and finally NXE's performance since January has been similar to CCJ's.
Despite these heavy losses, these large uranium stocks aren't really cheap. NXE and UEC have a negative EBITDA, CCJ is trading at a 40 EV/EBITDA ratio. LEU's EV is 20 times its EBITDA, which is better than the others but it is still not cheap. We are aware that CCJ has a large hidden asset, but the stock isn't a screaming buy.
The long-term potential of uranium miners is anchored by a structural, multi-decade macro thesis: a severe widening gap between surging demand and an inelastic supply pipeline. Uranium demand is shifting from linear growth to an accelerated release phase. Global uranium demand is projected to rise 28% by 2030 and nearly double by 2040. Investors know this which is why they are piling into early stage companies as well as currently unprofitable uranium stocks.
